# Animals and the Hound

## Animals belong in the story

> status: ratified (D-0064)

The author wants explicit animal elements — most concretely, the question of the
apprentice and a dog. Animals are part of the texture of a pre-modern world: droving,
herding, hunting, the household beast as survival infrastructure.

## The party's companion exists

> status: ratified (D-0040)

Whatever it turns out to be, the central party is "the three plus the wolf spirit
thing" — the author's own phrase. The companion is a full member of the found family
and one of the story's four exemplars of individual agency. Its file: [[hound]].

## Its nature is settled

> status: ratified (D-0116)

The companion is a Cù-Sìth/Gwyllgi-type moor-spirit — a minor landvættir in dog-shape of the
old animist order (D-0116). No one owns it; it works by consent, and it reads a storm or a
patrol long before any human can, though it never speaks. Its silence is twofold: the
reticence of a spirit, and a Wyrd fouled by a nearby mine's debt (the un-Tethered scar folded
in). The treaty is opened by patient, unpaid care — the apprentice draws a thorn from its paw
and combs the matted burrs from its coat, asking nothing — and sealed when they offer a woven
Frith-knot collar for the hound to accept; a shared half-ration first earns the approach.
Being a spirit, it can be the still-living witness the narrator's order reads centuries on
([[narrator]], D-0117).

## Consent-based companionship

> status: proposed

The session's sketch, never ruled on: in a Frith-governed world, "ownership" of an
animal is an imperial concept. The native way is negotiated partnership — aid and
rations exchanged for senses and presence, revocable by either side. The hound (if a
spirit) would understand proofs but not speak, act as early warning for storms and
patrols, choose the apprentice, tolerate the anchor, and regard the protagonist with
the wary respect due to something that smells like many people at once.

## The two regimes
> status: provisional (D-0088, D-0089)

Two incompatible laws govern beasts, and the difference is the class war in miniature.
The imperial regime treats animals as unregistered biomass to be brought onto the
rolls: a suppression-mark — the Tether — is carved or branded into hoof, horn, or hide,
a geas that dulls a creature's Wyrd and binds its will to its owner's account. The tell
is silence: in imperial territory the tethered beasts are unnaturally quiet, the animal
equivalent of a factory floor. The native regime, under Frith, recognizes no ownership
at all — only treaty. A working animal is a sovereign party that has agreed, and the
agreement is renewed by ongoing daily consent; it can be withdrawn by either side. This
is the reciprocity-versus-extraction fault line of [[wyrd-and-frith]] and the
[[allegory]], read at the scale of a single ox or hound.

## Animals as co-processors
> status: provisional (D-0088, D-0089, D-0180)

Magical animals are not familiars or spell-batteries; they are biological co-processors
in the extended-cognition sense of [[artifacts-and-memory]]. Their value is sensory: a
beast that can hear an axiom beginning to rot, or smell a Wyrd-storm a day out, supplies
physical signals a trained human translates into proof-variables. The animal senses; the
human reasons; the pair reasons better than either alone. This keeps animals inside the
story's thesis — cooperative cognition beats the isolated genius — without granting them
speech or spellcraft of their own.
Under D-0180, this is an interface into the one proof-system: the animal may witness,
sense, warn, consent, or refuse, but does not cast.

## The hierarchy of beasts
> status: provisional (D-0088, D-0089)

Three tiers, and the boundaries matter. Mundane fauna sit at the bottom and are the
first victims of axiomatic debt — the herds that sicken, the birds that vanish from a
poisoned valley — the ecological canaries of the collapse. Above them stand the apex
Wyrd-beasts: ancient, rare, effectively the earth's immune response, nearer to
landvættir than to animals. The protagonist neither hunts nor commands these; she kneels
and addresses them in the highest register of logic, as one sovereign head of state to
another. And a hard line sits outside the hierarchy entirely: monsters are not animals.
A monster is corrupted math made flesh, a proof gone malignant; confronting one is
debugging, not hunting, and it carries none of the ethical weight of killing a living
creature ([[anomalies]]).

## The hound as climate refugee
> status: provisional (D-0089)

The party's hound is framed as a Cù-Sìth / Gwyllgi-type moor hound displaced by ruin:
starving, mud-matted, its Wyrd fouled by the debt of a nearby mine — a climate refugee
on four legs, discarded by the same economy that discards people. Its bond with the
apprentice is not taming but shared survival, and the interface between them is a woven
Frith-knot collar that reads as a treaty-token, not a leash: nobody commands the hound,
and it works only with the one who honors the treaty.

The nature is now ratified as exactly this reading — a Cù-Sìth/Gwyllgi moor-spirit (D-0116;
see "Its nature is settled" above). The climate-refugee framing is the provisional texture
around that fixed core: the specific starving, mine-fouled condition is D-0089's AI-authored
substance and remains mutable, while the spirit-nature and the treaty rite are settled.

## Why the bond (sketches)
> status: proposed

Unratified motivations for why the apprentice, specifically, is bound to the hound — it
is a mutual-aid pact between two beings the empire filed as disposable, not a child with
a pet. Four strands:

- **Shared trauma of the discarded.** Both are refugees of the empire's arithmetic;
  together they are a two-node rebellion against the Ledger, each proof that the
  discarded can still choose.
- **An anchor of objective truth.** A hound cannot lie or commit a fallacy. For a
  hyper-vigilant child who has learned to distrust human words, a growl is a trustworthy
  reading of the world; when the hound judges the night safe and sleeps, the apprentice
  can finally sleep too.
- **Biological RAM.** The apprentice, still unschooled, reads the hound's ears, whine,
  hackles, and collar-knots as raw environmental signal — an organic, decentralized
  magic running alongside the protagonist's academic, centralized kind.
- **The daily rejection of the Tether.** Every shared ration and every burr picked out
  of the fur by hand renews the consent-treaty; the protagonist recognizes this small
  maintenance as the oldest and most radical form of ecology.

One thing is left open in the source and is not settled here: what exact first offering
or act of labor initiates the treaty with a starving, paranoid hound. It sits alongside
the hound's unresolved nature (Q-0006).
